Link is pretty stable and almost idiot proof on setup and usage,I give it 9/10,sometimes it loses the wifi connection (wifi is shit in my house), and requires going to the computer to bring the already running game back to fullscreen.Thats annoying,but uncommon.

Nothing, but not everyone puts their computer(s) in the living room. If your wireless N/AC connection is stable (this is a big if) it can and does do what's advertised wirelessly. Of course, a wired connection will always be better.

There's no need for it to be in the living room. I had a usb/hdmi going from the office to the living room. When you want to game on the tv swap the hdmi from your monitor to the one that goes to the TV and you're good to go. The one catch is you might need USB/HDMI repeaters if it's a particularly long distance but they're cheap.
... or you could just buy a steamlink and do it all in one device.

I highly recommend ethernet over powerline adapters. You can pick up a pair for under $50 (sometimes for $35). I've got one connected to my main router. I've got the remote one connected to a second router in my living room. That gives me what basically amounts to a second router with 4 ports and wireless. The main reason I've done this is that I want a fast connection for my XBox One, but I also have various streaming boxes. Although it's not theoretically as fast as a wired connection, in real-world use the performance is comparable.

I've had 3 pairs of these, all of them broke after a few months without being touched after the initial setup, they just wouldn't sync up with each other anymore, none of them lasted longer than 4 months, third pair I got were broken after 1. The power lines in my house is 70-80 years old or so though, except parts of it having been changed during renovations, guess that might have something to do with it, but I've never had issues with other electronic devices. Ended up getting a wireless repeater instead, since the issue was a bad wireless connection to the room my computer is in, its not as stable as the powerline adapters when they actually worked, but the repeater is 2 years old now.

That stinks that you had a bad experience with the adapters. I've used them (successfully) in 2 houses. The first house was built in 1940 and the other was built in the 60s. I've used 2 different brands--the first was Panasonic and my current ones are TP-Link. Both have worked flawlessly for me. I think I tried them in somebody else's house and they didn't work--like you alluded to, they're supposed to be on the same circuit (?)...I know you're not supposed to use them with power strips or surge protectors either (but I have). Obviously this doesn't apply to you since you've already had a bad experience, but for anybody else out there who hasn't tried ethernet over powerline adapters, they often work flawlessly and are worth checking out if your only other options are wi-fi or laying an extremely long CAT5/6 cable.
